newsitem.title: USA: More rain for Ohio River Valley, snow in Dakotas.
newsitem.headline: More rain for Ohio River Valley, snow in Dakotas.

text.p: More rain was forecast for the flooded Ohio River Valley this weekend and more snow was due in the Dakotas and northwest Minnesota early next week, meteorologists said.

An eastbound storm system, now in the southern Plains, should reach Tennessee and Kentucky this weekend producing 0.25 to 1.50 inches of rain. Tim Bowden, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc, said rain amounts may range from 0.50 to 1.50 inches with isolated areas receiving two inches.
"It won't help," said Bowden, of the rain's impact of flooding there.
Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp, expects lesser amounts probably 0.25 to 0.75 inch concentrated from Paducah, Ky., to Louisville.
The Ohio River flood is the worst in 33 years with water levels reaching rooftops. The river level was expected to drop this weekend from its 64.7-foot crest barring more rain.
After this weekend's rain system, both meteorologists expect dry conditions most of next week in the Ohio River Valley, with a cold front likely late next week.
Residents of the Dakotas and Minnesota can expect more snow early next week on top of the nearly one to three feet already on the ground.
WSC's Burgio expects light to moderate snowfall in the Dakotas and eastern Minnesota, with more likely later in the week.
Bowden said snow amounts could range from five to 10 inches beginning late Tuesday with rain in Nebraska and Iowa.
Burgio said 34 inches remains on the ground at Grand Forks in northeast North Dakota and four inches at Dickenson in the southwest.
Rain was forecast for the Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas this weekend with amounts from 0.25 to one inch south, Burgio said.
